evidence.support_text: In the Magnusson and Kligman test at reduced concentrations, cinnamic aldehyde/euglim 10:7:3 (mixture of cinnamic aldehyde, eugenol, limonene 10:7:3 v/v) tested at induction injection 0.03% and challenge 1.5% resulted in 2/10 animals positive with a mean erythema score of 0.6, indicating a positive skin sensitization response.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1% (vehicle not specified); 10 male albino guinea pigs
evidence.support_text: In a Magnusson-Kligman maximization test, cinnamyl alcohol at 1% produced no sensitization reactions in 10 guinea pigs, with no cross-reactions.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 120 mg/ml in ethanol, 20 female albino Ssc:AL guinea pigs
evidence.support_text: In a Magnusson-Kligman maximization test, cinnamic acid at 120 mg/ml in ethanol was tested in 20 female albino Ssc:AL guinea pigs and produced 1/20 reactions; no cross-reactions when challenged with cinnamic aldehyde and cinnamyl alcohol.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 120 mg/ml in ethanol; 20 female albino Ssc:AL guinea pigs
evidence.support_text: In a Magnusson-Kligman maximization test, cinnamic acid at 120 mg/ml in ethanol produced 1 sensitization reaction out of 20 guinea pigs, with no cross-reactions.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 120 mg/ml in ethanol; 20 female albino Ssc:AL guinea pigs
evidence.support_text: In a Magnusson-Kligman maximization test, cinnamyl alcohol at 120 mg/ml in ethanol produced 9 sensitization reactions out of 19 guinea pigs, with 15/20 cross-reactions to cinnamaldehyde.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 3.0% in petrolatum, outbred albino female Dunkin-Hartley guinea pigs
evidence.support_text: In a Magnusson-Kligman maximization test, cinnamaldehyde at 3.0% in petrolatum was tested in outbred albino female Dunkin-Hartley guinea pigs and produced 4/5 reactions with induction concentrations of 0.03% (intradermal) and 0.3% (topical); 5/5 reactions at all other dose levels.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 8 mg/ml in ethanol, albino female guinea pigs (Ssc:AL)
evidence.support_text: In a Magnusson-Kligman maximization test, cinnamaldehyde at 8 mg/ml in ethanol was tested in albino female guinea pigs (Ssc:AL) and produced 17/20 reactions, with 15/20 cross-reactions when challenged with cinnamyl alcohol and 7/20 cross-reactions when challenged with cinnamic acid.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 9 mg/ml in ethanol, 20 female albino Ssc:AL guinea pigs
evidence.support_text: In a Magnusson-Kligman maximization test, cinnamic acid at 9 mg/ml in ethanol was tested in 20 female albino Ssc:AL guinea pigs and produced no reactions (0/20) and no cross-reactions when challenged with cinnamic aldehyde and cinnamyl alcohol.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 9 mg/ml in ethanol; 20 female albino Ssc:AL guinea pigs
evidence.support_text: In a Magnusson-Kligman maximization test, cinnamic acid at 9 mg/ml in ethanol produced no sensitization reactions in 20 guinea pigs, and no cross-reactions.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 20 male Hartley guinea pigs, 300–500 g; induction: 4 occluded topical patches of 2% cinnamaldehyde in petrolatum to abraded shoulder skin, one every other day, with intradermal FCA at fourth application; challenge: occluded patch of 2% cinnamaldehyde in petrolatum on day 20 on flank; reactions read at 24, 48, 72 h.
evidence.support_text: Cinnamaldehyde was tested in a second Maguire (1973) skin sensitization study using 20 male Hartley guinea pigs weighing 300–500 g. Induction and challenge concentrations were both 2% cinnamaldehyde in petrolatum. Induction consisted of 4 occluded topical patches, one every other day, to abraded skin in the shoulder region. At the fourth application, an intradermal injection with FCA is made at the same test site in the shoulder region. An occluded challenge application was made on day 20 at a new and distant site on the clipped flank. Reactions were read 24, 48 and 72 h after application. Sensitization was observed in all 20 animals (Prince and Prince, 1977).

evidence.experimental_conditions: A subirritant concentration in petrolatum, male and female outbred Himalayan guinea pigs
evidence.support_text: Benzyl cinnamate was tested in a guinea pig maximization test at a subirritant concentration in petrolatum on male and female outbred Himalayan guinea pigs, and sensitization was observed (Klecak et al., 1977).

evidence.experimental_conditions: A subirritant concentration in petrolatum, male and female outbred Himalayan guinea pigs
evidence.support_text: Methyl cinnamate was tested in a guinea pig maximization test at a subirritant concentration in petrolatum on male and female outbred Himalayan guinea pigs, and sensitization effects were observed (Klecak et al., 1977).

evidence.experimental_conditions: CF-1 female mice; induction: clipping/tap stripping, intradermal FCA injection, then 100 µl of 10% cinnamaldehyde in ethanol applied for 3 consecutive days; challenge: 20 µl of 10% cinnamaldehyde in ethanol to right ear 7 days after final induction; ear swelling measured at 24 and 48 h with micrometer; criteria: test ear ≥20% greater thickness than control ear.
evidence.support_text: In a mouse ear swelling test (MEST) with CF-1 female mice, cinnamaldehyde at 10% in ethanol for induction and challenge produced ear swelling in 30% of animals, exceeding the 20% threshold for classification as a sensitizer.

evidence.assay_type: Modified Draize guinea pig sensitization test
evidence.experimental_conditions: 10 Dunkin-Hartley guinea pigs/dose; induction: intradermal injection of 0.5% cinnamaldehyde (vehicle not specified); challenge: topical application of 0.5% cinnamaldehyde (vehicle not specified) at 2 weeks and 3 weeks; reactions read at 24 and 48 h; repeat procedure if no sensitization.
evidence.support_text: Cinnamaldehyde was tested in a modified sensitization study (Draize, 1959) in Dunkin–Hartley guinea pigs (10/dose). Guinea pigs were treated by intradermal injection with 0.5% cinnamaldehyde (vehicle not specified) to induce sensitization followed 2 weeks later by a topical challenge with 0.5% cinnamaldehyde (vehicle not specified) and by a second challenge application one week after the initial challenge application. The entire induction and challenge procedure was repeated if there was no evidence of sensitization. Reactions to challenge were read at 24 and 48 h. No sensitization reactions were observed (Basketter and Allenby, 1991a).

evidence.assay_type: Modified Draize guinea pig sensitization test
evidence.experimental_conditions: 10 male and female Hartley guinea pigs, avg 350 g; induction: 0.1 ml intradermal 0.625% cinnamaldehyde (vehicle not reported) at 4 sites near axillary and inguinal lymph nodes; challenge day 14: intradermal 0.25% cinnamaldehyde (vehicle not reported) and topical open 20% cinnamaldehyde (vehicle not reported); reactions at 24 h; second challenge 7 days later; test repeated if no sensitization.
evidence.support_text: Sensitization potential was measured in a guinea pig sensitization study using a modified Draize procedure. Male and female inbred Hartley strain albino guinea pigs (10 per group) with an average weight of 350 g were shaved on both flanks. A 0.1 ml aliquot of 0.625% cinnamaldehyde (vehicle not reported) was injected intradermally at 4 sites that overlap the 2 auxiliary and 2 inguinal lymph nodes. The guinea pigs were challenged 14 days later by an intradermal injection of 0.25% cinnamaldehyde (vehicle not reported) into one flank and a topical open application of 20% cinnamaldehyde (vehicle not reported) on the other flank. Reactions were scored 24 h after challenge treatments. A second challenge was carried out 7 days later. If no sensitization reactions were observed, the test was repeated. Sensitization was observed after 2 sensitization treatments (Sharp, 1978).

evidence.assay_type: Modified Maguire guinea pig sensitization test
evidence.experimental_conditions: 20 male Hartley guinea pigs, 300–500 g; induction: 0.2 ml of 2% cinnamaldehyde in petrolatum rubbed onto 2 cm^2 abraded shoulder skin, 4 applications over one week; day 5 intradermal FCA on opposite side; challenge: occluded 2% cinnamaldehyde in petrolatum on day 20 on flank; reactions read at 24, 48, 72 h.
evidence.support_text: Cinnamaldehyde was tested in modified Maguire (1973) skin sensitization study using 20 male Hartley guinea pigs weighing 300–500 g. A 0.2 ml aliquot of 2% cinnamaldehyde in petrolatum was rubbed onto a 2 cm² area on clipped and abraded skin in the shoulder region. Four induction applications, one every other day, were made over a one-week period. An intradermal injection of FCA was made on day 5 on the opposite side from the test site. An occluded challenge application with 2% cinnamaldehyde in petrolatum was made on day 20 at a new and distant site on the clipped flank. Reactions were read 24, 48 and 72 h after application. Sensitization was observed in all 15/20 animals (Prince and Prince, 1977).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Dunkin-Hartley guinea pigs; intradermal induction with 0.015% cinnamaldehyde (vehicle not specified); 12 days later 6 h occluded challenge with 0.75% cinnamaldehyde (vehicle not specified); reactions read 22 and 46 h after patch removal.
evidence.support_text: In a second MSIAT test, cinnamaldehyde at 0.015% for induction and 0.75% for challenge produced 2 sensitization reactions plus 1 questionable reaction out of 10 animals.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Daily ear application for 3 days in female BALB/c mice; tested concentrations 0.825% to 6.25% v/v; a statistically significant increase was noted at 6.25%.
evidence.support_text: Although SI3 was not achieved, dermal treatment with 6.25% 1-butyl-1-methylpyrrolidinium chloride (BMPY) increased (p ≤ 0.01) lymph node cell proliferation in the LLNA.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Daily ear application for 3 days in female BALB/c mice; tested concentrations 3.12% to 12.5% v/v; a statistically significant increase was noted at 12.5%.
evidence.support_text: Although SI3 was not achieved, dermal treatment with 12.5% 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium chloride (BMIM) increased (p ≤ 0.01) lymph node cell proliferation in the LLNA.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Daily ear application for 3 days in female BALB/c mice; tested concentrations 6.25% to 50% v/v.
evidence.support_text: 1-Ethyl-3-methylimidazolium chloride (EMIM, 6.25% to 50% v/v) was neither an irritant nor a sensitizer in the primary irritancy/LLNA, indicating a negative LLNA result for skin sensitization.

evidence.experimental_conditions: DMAPA in dimethylformamide, 25 µL daily for 3 consecutive days on the dorsum of both ears of female CBA/Ca mice, intravenous 20 µCi [3H]methyl thymidine 5 days after initial treatment, lymph node cell precipitation with TCA, radioactivity measured by liquid scintillation.
evidence.support_text: In the LLNA study, the estimated concentration for a stimulation index of 3 (EC3) for DMAPA in dimethylformamide was 1.7%.

evidence.support_text: In contrast to PYR, data from the LLNA (and IRR and MEST) suggested that the contact sensitization potential of 5-amino-o-cresol (AOC) was minimal, indicating a negative classification in the LLNA.

evidence.support_text: The local lymph node assay (LLNA) results demonstrated that PYR is a sensitizer in female BALB/c mice when applied dermally using the LLNA with 25 µl to the dorsum of each ear on days 1,2,3 and ³H-thymidine incorporation measured on day 6. The criteria for a positive was at least one concentration with a stimulation index (SI) ≥3, statistically significant and dose-responsive. PYR was classified as a sensitizer.

evidence.experimental_conditions: LLNA in female CBA/Ca mice; 25 µL of 5% (v/v) glutaraldehyde in acetone applied to dorsum of each ear daily for 3 consecutive days; 5 days after initiation, IV injection of ³H-methyl thymidine; lymph node cell proliferation measured by β-scintillation; stimulation index calculated relative to vehicle (acetone) control.
evidence.support_text: Glutaraldehyde provoked a very vigorous response in the LLNA using acetone as vehicle; a stimulation index of approximately 18 was achieved with the highest concentration tested (5% v/v).

evidence.experimental_conditions: LLNA in female CBA/Ca mice; concentrations of glutaraldehyde at 0.25%, 0.5%, 1%, and 2.5% (v/v) in acetone applied to dorsum of each ear daily for 3 consecutive days; 5 days after initiation, IV injection of ³H-methyl thymidine; lymph node cell proliferation measured by β-scintillation; stimulation index calculated relative to vehicle (acetone) control.
evidence.support_text: Glutaraldehyde, when examined using acetone as vehicle, provoked a very vigorous response, with all but the lowest concentration tested (0.1%) inducing stimulation indices of 3 or greater.

evidence.experimental_conditions: LLNA in mice; test compound applied at concentrations up to 50% v/v in 50% ethanol vehicle; ear application; EC3 calculated from dose-response.
evidence.support_text: The soluble MWF TRIM VX (EC3 = 6.9%) was identified to induce a 3-fold increase in lymphocyte proliferation in the LLNA; significant proliferation was observed after exposure to 25% TRIM VX.

evidence.experimental_conditions: LLNA-ELISA (BrdU incorporation) in BALB/c mice; ear application of test substance
evidence.support_text: LLNA was performed with BALB/c mice treated with p-phenylenediamine (PPD, positive control), bee venom (BV), or PLA2-free bee venom (PBV). In all PPD concentrations, stimulation indexes (SI) were ≥1.6, determined to be sensitizer, while SI levels of BV and PBV were below 1.6. Based on these findings, both BV and PBV are proposed as nonsensitizers.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Male mice; topical dosing on ears with 25 µl/day for 3 days; vehicle: 3:1 EtOH:DEP; concentrations 0.1–10% w/v; cinnamaldehyde exposed to air for 8 weeks (simulating manufacturing exposure); stabilized with antioxidants (0.1 and 2% d,l-α-tocopherol, 0.1% Trolox C, mixture of 0.3% BHT/d,l-α-tocopherol/eugenol) or unstabilized; 2 days rest; i.v. ³HTdR on day 6; LNCs harvested 5 h later; SI calculation; EC3 by linear interpolation.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Mice exposed to 0.5–10% compound 1 in the LLNA. Stimulation indices (SI) were 0.69 (0.5%), 0.85 (1%), 0.76 (2.5%), 0.66 (5%), 0.77 (10%). Positive control α-hexylcinnamaldehyde (25%) gave SI 8.58.
evidence.support_text: Mice exposed to 0.5–10% compound 1 showed no increase in ear swelling relative to vehicle and no increase in lymph node cell proliferation at any concentration tested, with stimulation indices (SI) all below 1 (e.g., 0.77 at 10%). In contrast, the known sensitizer α-hexylcinnamaldehyde (HCA) produced an SI of 8.58. The authors concluded that compound 1 did not induce delayed contact hypersensitivity and was non-irritant.
